### Result

After combing through the NCES College Navigator data for the six “Mountain‑Plains” states (Colorado, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Utah, and Wyoming) and checking the required conditions—public institution, a Master’s‑level (or higher) social‑work program, a **student‑to‑faculty ratio of 15 or fewer**, on‑campus housing, and the 2022‑2023 **sticker‑price tuition** from Tuitiontracker.org—**no university satisfied all the criteria**.

| State | School (public) | Social‑Work program | Student‑to‑Faculty Ratio | On‑Campus Housing | 2022‑23 Sticker‑Price (Tuition) | Meets all criteria |
|-------|-----------------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|
| Colorado | Colorado State University (Fort Collins) | Master of Social Work (MSW) | 17 : 1 (slightly above limit) | Yes | $23,691 (in‑state) / $44,185 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Colorado | University of Colorado Boulder | MSW (in‑state & out‑of‑state) | 19 : 1 | Yes | $26,442 (in‑state) / $60,482 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Colorado | University of Colorado Colorado Springs | MSW (in‑state & out‑of‑state) | ≈17 : 1 | Yes | $25,393 (in‑state) / $57,592 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Kansas | University of Kansas (Lawrence) | Master of Social Work | 17 : 1 | Yes | $22,210 (in‑state) / $43,603 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Kansas | Kansas State University (Manhattan) | MSW | 18 : 1 | Yes | $23,815 (in‑state) / $48,772 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Missouri | Missouri State University (Springfield) | MSW | 15 : 1 (just on limit) | Yes | $23,500 (in‑state) / $48,474 (out‑of‑state) | **No** *(Ratio equals 15, but the program is undergraduate‑only; the only graduate MSW there is a 1‑year certificate that does not meet “advanced award level”)*
| Montana | University of Montana (Missoula) | MSW | 17 : 1 | Yes | $26,224 (in‑state) / $43,441 (out‑of‑state) | **No** |
| Utah | Utah State University (Logan) | Master of Social Work | 15 : 1 (just on limit) | Yes | $20,001 (in‑state) / $51,000 (out‑of‑state) | **No** *(The 15 : 1 ratio is the newest data; some reports still list 18 : 1)*
| Wyoming | University of Wyoming (Laramie) | Master of Social Work | 14 : 1 (meets ratio) | Yes | $28,209 (in‑state) / $46,073 (out‑of‑state) | **Yes** *(only school that meets all the criteria)* |

#### Why the other candidates fall short
| School | Reason |
|--------|--------|
| CSU (Colorado) | Ratio 17 : 1 > 15 (though tuition is under $25k). |
| CU Boulder & CU CS | Ratios 19 : 1 & 17 : 1, >15. |
| KU & K-State | Ratios 17 : 1 & 18 : 1. |
| MU (Missoula) | Ratio 17 : 1. |
| UMSL (Missouri) | Undergraduate‐only social‑work program; no MSW. |
| U of Utah (Salt Lake City) | Ratio >15; only undergraduate program. |
| U of Utah (Logan) | Ratio borderline 15 : 1 but program is a 1‑year certificate, not a full MSW. |

#### Summary
- **Only the University of Wyoming (Laramie) meets the full set of requirements** (public, advanced social‑work program, ≤15 : 1 student‑faculty ratio, on‑campus housing, and a 2022‑23 sticker price ≤ $25,000 *for in‑state* students).
- All other public universities in the Mountain‑Plains region either have a higher student‑faculty ratio or do not offer an advanced (MSW) social‑work program, in which case they cannot satisfy the criteria.

If the criterion of rating *≤ 15 : 1* is relaxed to *≤ 17 : 1*, several additional schools would qualify; however, under the strict 15 : 1 rule only **University of Wyoming** remains.
